newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican leftists shot at in run-up to elections.
newsitem.headline: Mexican leftists shot at in run-up to elections.

text.p: Two truckloads of Mexican leftists were shot at and harassed in the southern state of Oaxaca in a sign of mounting strife ahead of elections in July, a main opposition party said on Tuesday.

Saul Vicente, head of the leftist Democratic Revolution Party (PRD) in Oaxaca, said Monday's attack was carried out by supporters of the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) in an area where a PRD activist and three family members were shot dead last week.
He said the attack occured in the coastal town of San Agustin Chayuco, some 120 miles (200 km) southeast of the state capital.
Vicente said the attackers opened fire on the trucks, missing the occupants, and then beat up the town's PRD leader who was one of the passengers.

Later that night, "the PRI guys headed by their municipal authorities went round the town, pulling down party propaganda. They then used loud speakers threatening death to anyone who dares to vote for the PRD," Vicente told reporters.

The country goes to the polls on July 6 in mid-term elections to vote in a new Congress. The PRD, which is Mexico's third party, has been growing in popularity, especially in poor areas, according to pollsters.
The PRI has ruled Mexico for 68 years.
